title: Shooting 'ruined' birthday
article: "Fearless, Painless, Senseless," read one tattoo in large gothic letters across Sand's belly. A satanic head smoking a joint was on his left shoulder.

Sand, 20, was shot dead by an RCMP sniper on Dec. 21, 2001, at a motel in Wolseley, Sask. The shooting came 14 hours after Sand, his brother Robert and Robert's lover Laurie Bell are alleged to have rammed an RCMP cruiser in Russell, Man., then shot to death Const. Dennis Strongquill, a 20-year police veteran.
Robert Sand, 24, and Bell, 21, are on trial for the first-degree murder of Strongquill.

The day Danny died was also Robert Sand's 23rd birthday. Const. Mel Zurevinsky testified that after Robert was arrested, he complained to his captors: "You ruined my birthday. You killed my brother on my birthday."
At the motel, Danny climbed on the roof with a high-powered rifle as the RCMP encircled the building.
He had smoked marijuana anywhere from 12 minutes to four hours before the time of his death, testified RCMP toxicologist John Hudson.

Marijuana can alter perceptions and reduce inhibitions, Hudson told the Brandon jury. If a person on marijuana were in a dangerous situation, that person might not be able to process all the information.

In Danny's pockets, police found 15 rounds of ammunition for a 270 Winchester rifle. Along with a massive wound to Danny's head, inflicted by the sniper, there were gunshots wounds to his arm and his upper back, which Crown prosecutor Bob Morrison said occurred when Strongquill's partner Brian Auger fired on the Sand brothers and Bell in Russell.

Robert Sand was unharmed and unarmed at the time of his arrest. He was polite during his arrest, Zurevinsky testified. When the police loosened off a handcuff that he'd complained was too tight on a sore wrist, Robert said: "Thanks for being gentle taking off the handcuffs."
The Crown says Bell and the Sand brothers committed crimes in Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba in the days leading up to the killing.
The trial is expected to last until the end of June.
